rubric.name: Commit message review
rubric.description: Is this a good commit message?
rubric.context: You review one commit message from an open-source Java project.

anchors.no: Nothing in the message, stated or implied, gives a reason for the change and there is no issue or pull request reference
anchors.yes: The message gives a reason, in any one of these ways: describes the issue (error scenario, shortcoming, issue report); states the objective or goal; illustrates a requirement (something out of date, environment changed, a usage need); implies necessity (follows a convention, brings an improvement or benefit, relates to an implemented feature or prior commit); or references the issue or pull request the change belongs to

anchors.no: The message describes only the problem, symptom or desired outcome and never says which change was made
anchors.yes: The message says what was changed, even briefly: naming the object of change and the kind of change (add, remove, update, rename, polish, fix in a named file or component) is enough. A change list, a before/after contrast, what the code now does, or how the change works also count

inputs.text:
Disallow all extensions in actuator endpoints (except .json)

Along with the recent change in Spring to use content-disposition
'inline' (which prevents the download), it also makes sense to limit
the extensions allowed by the actuator endpoints. Really there *is*
no extension for these endpoints, but since all of them explicitly
produce JSON we can add .json for browsers as a convenience in case
the app would otherwise choose to send XML.

Fixes gh-4402
